risk.premise_issue: The scenario describes a simultaneous Category 6 cyclone (420 km/h) and Moment Magnitude 11.5 earthquake, both of which are physically impossible: (1) The Saffir-Simpson scale only defines Categories 1-5; Category 6 does not exist, and 420 km/h exceeds the highest reliably recorded tropical cyclone wind speeds (~345 km/h). (2) The largest earthquake ever recorded was Mw 9.5 (1960 Valdivia); Mw 11.5 would require a fault rupture orders of magnitude larger than Earth's tectonic plates allow. No historical precedent exists for such a compound event.

briefing.executive_summary: The scenario describes a simultaneous Category 6 cyclone (420 km/h) and Moment Magnitude 11.5 earthquake in Tokyo, Japan. All three specialist agents verify this scenario is physically impossible: the Saffir-Simpson scale only defines Categories 1-5 (maximum reliably recorded winds ~345 km/h), and the largest earthquake ever recorded was Mw 9.5 (1960 Valdivia). An Mw 11.5 event would require a fault rupture larger than Earth's tectonic plates allow. No historical precedent exists for such a compound event. Historical earthquake data for Japan (1900-2030) shows median 2 deaths, p90 49 deaths, median 3,535 affected, p90 120,800 affected, median damage $525M, p90 $19.5B (n=21-31 events). Current Tokyo weather: 9.7°C, 71% humidity, 4.7 km/h wind, no precipitation.
action_plan: Acknowledge scenario is physically impossible; no operational disaster response can be planned for impossible hazards.
Reference historical Japanese earthquake baselines (median 2 deaths, p90 49 deaths) for realistic contingency planning.
Ensure any future scenario uses physically plausible parameters (max Category 5 cyclone, max ~Mw 9.5 earthquake).
Collect exposed population, shelter capacity, and water inventory data for Tokyo to enable meaningful logistics/evacuation analysis for plausible scenarios.
